contract: The solver builds a per-campaign click accounting module. Each click is recorded once with a frozen disposition (late, fraud, invalid or billed), counted into 60-unit tumbling windows with a joint geo and device breakdown, and billed only when valid and not fraudulent. An explicit per-campaign watermark closes windows 120 units after they end. Reads return one request's audit record, one window, or the populated windows in a range.

study.title: Ad-Click Aggregation
study.reason: The case study's deduplicated event-time accounting with late events maps directly to campaign-scoped request idempotence, watermark-driven window closure and pre-aggregated window counters.

pstates.name: $$campaigns
pstates.schema: {String fixed-keys{watermark, requests: subindexed map of audit records, windows: subindexed map of window start to totals plus subindexed geo/device breakdown}}

topologies.name: click-accounting
topologies.does: advances watermarks, assigns dispositions, writes audit records and bumps window counters

topologies.name: windows-in-range
topologies.does: pages sorted windows in a range and reads each returned breakdown

design.ownership: Campaign id is the depot hash key and the query |hash key, so all request and window state for a campaign sits on one task. The replay check, disposition, audit write and counter update happen together with no cross-partition hop.

stated: Every click is recorded exactly once; replays have no effect
Bounded work per click, independent of clicks, windows or campaigns
get-windows work is proportional to windows and breakdown entries returned
Reads of one campaign do not read other campaigns' state
Durable Rama state; runs with 2 and 4 tasks; per-campaign ordering

tested.nfr: Point read and click cost under growth
tested.mechanism: Event hook counts RocksDB reads and iterator reads for get-request, get-window and counted, late and replayed clicks, before and after adding 150 windows, 100 late audits and 12 other campaigns; bound is 2x plus 20
get-windows over a fixed 3-window range as out-of-range windows grow from 700 to 2,900
Read cost of a counted click as the target window's breakdown grows from 128 to 512 pairs
Replayed request ids leave audit and counters unchanged, including across campaigns
Module update in the same JVM, then state is read back

gaps.gap: get-window cost is measured only on windows holding 3 to 5 clicks
gaps.wrongDesign: Store raw clicks per window and sum totals and breakdown at read time; cost grows with clicks in the window and still passes

gaps.gap: Write amplification and task balance are unmeasured
gaps.wrongDesign: Rewrite a per-campaign summary on every click, or route every event through |global; reads stay flat so all tests pass
A stream topology that writes the audit record, then hops to bump counters; a retry sees the audit and skips the counters, losing the click

contract: The solver builds a multi-tenant metrics store keyed by tenant, metric and labels. Each series has a monotonic logical clock that decides whether a sample is accepted as new or rejected as future, expired or duplicate. Raw samples are kept for 300 clock units and folded into 60-unit and 3600-unit rollups kept for 7200 units past bucket end. Queries return raw samples or complete rollup buckets in a half-open range, plus per-series counters.

study.title: Metrics Pipeline
study.reason: The case study's time-series aggregation, downsampling tiers and retention map directly to raw samples, 60 and 3600 rollups and clock-driven expiry.

depots.name: *series-events
depots.partition: hash by series key [tenant metric labels]

pstates.name: $$series
pstates.schema: {SeriesKey fixed-keys{clock, admission counters, raw: subindexed timestamp->value, buckets-60: subindexed start->{count sum min max}, buckets-3600: small plain map}}

topologies.name: metrics
topologies.does: admits samples, folds both rollups and prunes expired keys on clock advance

topologies.name: query-raw
topologies.does: range-selects retained raw samples for one series

topologies.name: query-rollup
topologies.does: selects complete, retained buckets of one width in a range

design.ownership: The canonical series key is both the depot hash key and the query |hash key, so ingest, expiry and reads for a series stay on one task. No read or write touches another series.

stated: Queries do work proportional to the series' data inside the range only
ingest-sample! does bounded work; get-series-info examines bounded state
advance-clock! may work in proportion to what it expires, on that series only
Raw kept while ts + 300 > clock; rollups kept while start + width + 7200 > clock
Durable state; runs with 2 and 4 tasks

tested.nfr: Read and ingest cost under growth
tested.mechanism: Event hook counts RocksDB reads for query-raw, both rollup widths, get-series-info, ingest and a non-expiring clock advance, small vs grown; bound is 2x plus 20
A 3-bucket 60-width rollup must cost under 50 reads with 100 out-of-range buckets present
A large clock jump must cost under 8 times the expired-plus-retained count; upper bound only
Other series are untouched by a clock advance
Module update in the same JVM, then state is read back

gaps.wrongDesign: advance-clock! only writes the clock and queries clamp to the retention floor; expired data stays in RocksDB forever and every test passes

gaps.gap: No data sits above a query range
gaps.wrongDesign: Range reads that iterate from the start key to the end of the map pass, because growth is all below the range

gaps.gap: Write amplification, task balance and stream retries are untested
gaps.wrongDesign: Rewrite a whole non-subindexed bucket map per sample, route through |global, or double-count accepted under a stream retry

contract: The solver builds the durable core of a per-user API rate limiter with two token buckets per request: one for the user and one for the user and endpoint. Each request debits both buckets or neither, using exact integer refill per logical tick. Users own versioned configurations, including a shadow mode that accounts identically but never rejects. Decisions are idempotent per request id and readable later.

study.title: Distributed Rate Limiter
study.reason: The case study's token-bucket quota decisions map directly to atomic two-bucket debits and retry-safe consumption per request id.

pstates.name: $$users
pstates.schema: {String fixed-keys{limiter: version, config, clock, user bucket, endpoint buckets (up to 16); decisions: subindexed map of request id -> decision}}

topologies.name: core
topologies.does: applies configs, refills and debits both buckets, and records decisions

design.ownership: User id is the depot hash key and the PState key, so one user's buckets, clock and decisions live on one task. A single microbatch path there makes the two-bucket debit atomic with no cross-partition hop. Reads are direct point selects.

stated: check! is fixed work per request, independent of accumulated decisions
Numeric budgets: reads at most 4 point reads, 2 seeks, 8 iterator reads, 0 writes
Across 400 users, total writes 1x to 8x and per-task balance 0.5x to 1.5x
Atomic two-bucket debit; idempotent decisions per request id
Latency is explicitly not tested

tested.mechanism: Event hook counts reads at 32 vs 512 decisions against an absolute budget plus bounded growth, on user-owned PStates only
New, retried and denied checks measured with commit write counts against a write budget and growth bound
400 users across two clients with one thread per task; per-task writes and reads within 0.5x to 1.5x of the mean; reads write nothing

tested.nfr: Concurrent debits on a hot user
tested.mechanism: Two clients hit one user; debits sum exactly and tokens never go negative
Retried request ids, including with changed bodies across config versions, keep the first decision

gaps.wrongDesign: A stream topology that writes the debit before the decision record; a retry between the two finds no decision and debits again

gaps.gap: Whole-value blobs are invisible to count-based tests
gaps.wrongDesign: Store all decision history as one non-subindexed value; operation counts stay flat while bytes grow
Keep every request-id decision forever; storage grows without bound and no test notices

contract: The solver builds the durable core of a URL shortener with caller-supplied aliases. An alias maps to an immutable target URL with optional expiry and can never be created again, even after deletion. Owners can delete, block and unblock links, and resolve-alias reports status-aware results. A lifetime click counter counts trusted click observations once per click id.

study.title: URL Shortener
study.reason: The case study's unique aliases, link lifecycle and click accounting map directly to permanent alias reservation, lifecycle flags and deduplicated click counts.

pstates.name: $$links
pstates.schema: {String fixed-keys{link: target, expiry, deleted, blocked, clicks; outcomes: subindexed request id -> keyword; click-ids: subindexed set}}

topologies.name: core
topologies.does: creates, deletes, blocks and unblocks links and counts deduplicated clicks

design.ownership: Alias is the depot hash key and the PState key, so every command for an alias is point work on one task. Reads are direct point selects with no query topology and no cross-partition hop.

stated: Fixed-work reads and record-click!, independent of click and request history
Numeric read and write budgets, and balance across tasks
Workload: 100k resolves per second, viral aliases, 1M observations per alias
Exactly one created outcome among concurrent creates
Clicks deduplicated per alias and click id

tested.mechanism: Event hook counts reads for get-click-count, resolve-alias and outcomes at 32 vs 512 history, against an absolute budget plus growth
New and duplicate record-click! measured with commit write counts against a budget
400 aliases with one thread per task; per-task writes and reads within 0.5x to 1.5x; reads write nothing
Two clients create the same alias; exactly one gets created
Distinct click observations from two clients are all counted

gaps.wrongDesign: A stream topology that inserts the click id, then increments the count in a later step; a retry sees the id and skips, so the count is low

gaps.gap: Whole-value blobs are invisible to count-based tests
gaps.wrongDesign: Store all click ids for an alias as one non-subindexed set; counts stay flat while bytes grow

gaps.gap: Hot-alias click bursts are not measured directly
gaps.wrongDesign: A design whose per-click writes grow during a burst to one alias is caught only indirectly by the per-click budget

contract: The solver builds the durable core of a typeahead service. Each locale publishes generational corpus snapshots, and search events add session-deduplicated trend points on the current generation. A persistent blocklist is applied before top-k selection. suggest returns the top-k phrases for a prefix with exact scores and deterministic tie-breaking.

study.title: Search Autocomplete
study.reason: The case study's precomputed top-k per prefix, trending overlay and policy filtering map directly to locale snapshots, session-deduplicated trends and blocklist-filtered prefix ranking.

pstates.name: $$owner
pstates.key: locale; current generation at the owning task

pstates.name: $$generation
pstates.key: locale; replicated generation read by placed partitions

topologies.name: core
topologies.does: publishes snapshots, applies blocks and updates session-deduplicated trend ranks

topologies.name: suggest
topologies.does: hashes to the placed prefix partition and reads the first k ranked entries

topologies.name: phrase
topologies.does: hashes to the placed phrase partition and reads its score

design.ownership: The depot hashes by locale, but phrase and prefix work is placed by locale plus the first two characters and reached with |hash. A search updates long-prefix ranks at its own placement, then hops to the one-character prefix placement.

stated: suggest work is independent of matching candidates and corpus size; no scan at query time
record-search! does fixed work bounded by phrase length
publish-snapshot! scales with snapshot size, not the previous generation's trends
Fixed-work get-phrase and get-generation
Work and storage are balanced across tasks

tested.mechanism: suggest for a 2-character prefix at k=1 with 300 vs 3,000 phrases must cost under 4 times the small case
Read and commit write counts at 60 vs 600 sessions
Publish cost after 20 vs 320 prior-generation trending phrases
A 600-phrase hot prefix with the top 12 blocked must still return correct results
Module update in the same JVM, then state is read back

gaps.gap: Fixture score order equals lexical order
gaps.wrongDesign: Scan the prefix range lexically, capped at 1,000 entries, and return the best k; results are correct and cost stays under the 4x ratio

gaps.gap: Task balance is printed, not asserted
gaps.wrongDesign: Hash all work by locale so one locale sits on one task; tests use one locale and still pass
Keep every superseded generation's phrases, sessions and prefixes forever; the reference does this too
